official.deadline_central_display: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on course (all applicants outside the US round); US round: 14 October 2026
official.deadline_note: Two selection rounds. US citizens resident in the USA must apply by Wednesday 14 October 2026 (full application, including references, by 11:59pm UK time) and are not eligible for the later round. All other applicants apply by the Course Funding Deadline listed in the University Course Directory - either Tuesday 8 December 2026 or Wednesday 6 January 2027 - with all documents submitted by 11:59pm UK time. Applications opened 11 September 2026; outcomes by 14 December 2026 (US round) or 8 March 2027 (International round); offers by early February 2027 or early April 2027 and must be accepted within 72 hours.
official.status_note: Applications for entry in the academic year 2027/8 are now open.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The University Composition Fee at the appropriate rate. The fee varies by student type and precise amounts are set out in the University's Graduate Studies prospectus; where a student gains a fee award from public authorities such as UKRI they should accept it and the Trust will not pay their fee or may share fee and maintenance costs.

official.description: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship covers the full cost of studying at Cambridge. Each year around 70 full-cost scholarships are awarded to outstanding applicants from countries outside the UK, in any subject, to build a global network of future leaders committed to improving the lives of others.
official.program_type: Full-cost postgraduate scholarship at the University of Cambridge
official.english_requirement: Cambridge sets the required score on each course page; accepted tests are IELTS (Academic), IELTS for UKVI Academic, IELTS One Skill Retake, IELTS Online, TOEFL iBT (including Home Edition) and, for some courses, C1 Advanced and C2 Proficiency. Scores from different certificates cannot be combined and results must be dated no more than 2 years before the course start date. Evidence is not usually needed until an offer (LLM and MCL applicants provide it at application). Exempt: nationals of majority English-speaking countries educated there, and holders of a 3-year qualification equivalent to a UK Bachelor's from a majority English-speaking country (excluding Canada) taken within 2 years of starting.

applicant_utility.summary: Gates Cambridge pays the University Composition Fee, a £23,152 maintenance allowance for 12 months, flights and visa costs, but the fee itself is assessed separately, so the package is worth far more than the stipend figure alone. Most applicants enter through the international round, which follows their course's funding deadline of either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, while US citizens resident in the USA face one earlier October deadline they cannot switch away from. Departments nominate only a handful of applicants, so the real filter happens before the Trust ever ranks you, and any offer must be accepted within 72 hours.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically exceptional non-UK citizens with a documented record of improving others' lives who want complete funding for a Cambridge PhD, MLitt or one-year master's.
application_readiness_checklist: Look up your exact course in the Cambridge Course Directory and note whether its funding deadline is 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027
Brief your Gates Cambridge referee on the four criteria and confirm they will submit well before the deadline
Draft the four selection questions around concrete examples rather than general statements
Prepare a research proposal if applying for a PhD, even if the admission application does not demand one
Book an English test early if you are not exempt; scores must be under 2 years old and cannot be combined across sittings
Tell the Trust immediately about any employer salary or other substantial scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Not being nominated by the Cambridge department - comparatively few applicants pass this first filter
Selection-question answers that describe ambition but give no specific evidence of improving lives or leadership
A Gates reference that reads like a third academic reference instead of addressing the four criteria
References or documents arriving after the 11:59pm UK time deadline, which voids an otherwise strong case
Applying for an excluded course type such as an MBA, MASt or part-time non-PhD degree
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Bench fees and the cost of scientific equipment or similar academic resources are explicitly not covered and are expected to be met by the Cambridge department, and anything beyond the maintenance allowance - for example living costs above it, dependants' costs outside the discretionary allowance, or visa costs for family - must be funded personally.
document_audit: The Gates Cambridge reference is separate from your two academic references - brief that referee specifically on the four criteria
PhD applicants need a research proposal even where the admission application does not require one
English certificates are verified online; reports sent directly by IELTS or TOEFL are not accepted
English results cannot be pooled from different certificates and must be under 2 years old at course start
alerts: US citizens resident in the USA must apply by 14 October 2026 and are barred from the later international round
Scholarship offers must be accepted within 72 hours, so keep offer-window dates free in early February and early April
Receiving an employer salary or another substantial scholarship lets the Trust reduce or stop the maintenance allowance
Winning a public fee award such as UKRI means you must accept it, and the Trust may not pay your fee
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File one combined admission-and-funding application in the Graduate Application Portal; departments nominate a small shortlist, then nominees attend a 25-30 minute interview, in person where possible, before scholars are selected.

Departmental deadlines for putting candidates forward may fall earlier.

official.description: The President's PhD Scholarships offer 50 high-performing new PhD applicants full funding for tuition fees and a generous stipend for a 3.5-year PhD place at Imperial College London, alongside a consumables fund and cohort opportunities from the Early Career Researcher Institute.
official.program_type: Centrally funded doctoral scholarship scheme for new PhD entrants
official.english_requirement: Imperial sets a standard or higher English level per course. Standard: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in every element; higher: 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in every element. Equivalent accepted tests include Duolingo (115/125 overall), TOEFL iBT (92/100 overall), PTE Academic (62/69 overall) and LanguageCert Academic SELT (70/75), with results valid within 2 years of the course start date. Nationals may also qualify through accepted qualifications or exemption, or by passing the Imperial Pre-Sessional English Programme; doctoral students must also meet the Doctoral Academic Communication Requirement after entry.

applicant_utility.summary: Imperial's President's PhD Scholarships pay full tuition for 3.5 years plus a £27,036 (2027-28) annual stipend, a £2,000-a-year consumables fund for the first three years and ECRI development, but only 50 places exist and a department must nominate you before the College panel sees the file. There are three rounds a year - 2 November 2026, 11 January 2027 and 1 March 2027 - and the first round also secures the earliest funded start dates between 1 August and 1 November 2027. Applicants who miss out are automatically reconsidered for a standard PhD place, so the downside of applying is limited to the effort, not the admission itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates holding a first-class or integrated master's degree, or a master's distinction, who have already secured an Imperial supervisor and can evidence research potential.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm a supervisor has agreed in writing to supervise your project, then check the Unavailable Supervisors list for conflicts
Tick the President's PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the additional questions tab, or the application will not be considered
Build the personal statement as exactly two pages: motivation and background on page 1, research proposal on page 2
Check whether your course needs the standard or higher English level and hold a qualifying test within the 2-year validity window
Nominate two academic referees who are not your proposed supervisor and brief them on academic evidence
Ask the department for its internal deadline for putting candidates forward, which can fall before the round date
common_rejection_risks: Applying without an agreed supervisor, which is a hard requirement rather than a nice-to-have
Listing the proposed PhD supervisor as one of the two academic referees
A page-2 research proposal that is generic instead of matched to the department's strengths and the supervisor's work
Falling below first class or distinction without persuading the department to select you under the Department Special Case provision
Being cut at departmental shortlisting, since only shortlisted candidates ever reach the College Selection Panel
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package names no travel, relocation or visa funding, and the consumables fund covers only the first 3 of the 3.5 years, so relocation costs, visa expenses and late-stage research costs beyond the £2,000 annual fund sit with the student.
document_audit: The personal statement must be a 2-page document with the research proposal on page 2 - longer proposals belong in the separate research proposal upload
The proposed PhD supervisor cannot be used as a referee
Departments may add their own supporting-document requirements on top of the central instructions
English tests must be within 2 years of the intended start date, and IELTS single-element retakes are not accepted
alerts: Only new PhD applications count - current registered Imperial PhD students are barred from the scheme
Supervisors may hold only one President's scholar at a time, so your first-choice supervisor may already be unavailable
Missing all three round dates pushes funding consideration into the next academic year, since funded starts are limited to 1 August - 1 November 2027
Any PhD offer is conditional on achieving the predicted qualification
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the standard Imperial admissions application with the scholarship selected in the funding section; the department reviews and shortlists, a Faculty allocation stage may make initial offers, and the College Selection Panel makes the final decision.
